title: Professor Manetta as pianist and multi-instrumentalist
summary: She calls Manetta the best piano player in New Orleans; Allen and she discuss his instruments and why he never played bass.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So I've always been well chaperoned. Yeah. And at the time, though, that Emanuel was very popular with the piano, too. And he played the clarinet to give me a chance at the piano, you see. Oh, yeah. Yeah.

You know, he could play all the instruments, and he still does, too. Yeah, he does. Like the other one, there's two instruments at once. I wondered about his piano playing. I've only heard him, of course, the last six or seven years, really, a little longer, maybe. And I never did hear him like about 30 years ago when he used to play all the time. Did he play a much different style? Yes, yes.
He played the styles that had them.
Because he still gets around awfully well on the piano, doesn't he?
He has remarkable. I must say, not to brag about it, but he was the best New Orleans. That's what people have told. Really the best there was in New Orleans.
Because even today, he plays remarkably well. Yes, he do. He plays almost more piano than anyone you hear nowadays. When he gets going, good.
Did you hear him at the presentation hall?
I think he done real well with him.

And with his two instruments, I've heard him on guitar, too. I've heard him play those two pieces. He plays Dixie like he did on the piano, with Dixie in one hand and Yankee Doodle and the other. He does that on guitar, too. He mixes up the two tunes and keeps them going with the two fingers. And the Cardian, I've heard him play on that, too, very well.
Yeah, he play about every instrument. Yes, about everything. I never saw him play a bass. That's about the only one. No, that's right.
I never did either. No, I never did.

You see, bass tears up his fingers so much. You know, he gets such terrible cones. Yes. And he likes to preserve his fingers, too, you know. So I guess that's why he never bothered too much with the bass. But he could play it.
Well, I bet he could, too. Yeah, yeah. Bass horn and all.
